source: 45 of the 66 connection forms map onto the curated motif document (motifs/swarm_agent_topology_motifs.json); the other 21 are new forms introduced by this library.
caveat: Connection forms are qualitative taxonomies. `parameters` are literature-scale defaults for simulation, not fitted values.

connection_types.name: axo_dendritic
connection_types.description: Axon terminal onto dendritic shaft/spine; the default cortical excitatory contact.

connection_types.name: axo_somatic
connection_types.description: Axon terminal onto soma; perisomatic, strongly shunting (basket-cell style).

connection_types.name: axo_axonic
connection_types.description: Axon terminal onto the axon initial segment; gates spike initiation without touching the soma.

connection_types.name: dendro_dendritic
connection_types.description: Direct dendro-dendritic contact; allows subthreshold crosstalk and reciprocal pairs.

connection_types.name: axo_dendrite_reciprocal
connection_types.description: Reciprocal pair: one direction excitatory, the return direction inhibitory (olfactory-bulb style).
connection_types.biological_reference: Rall et al 1966; olfactory bulb mitral/granule pair

connection_types.name: pre_presynaptic_inhibition
connection_types.description: Inhibition applied to a presynaptic terminal; attenuates release downstream.

connection_types.name: pre_presynaptic_excitation
connection_types.description: Excitation applied to a presynaptic terminal; boosts release probability.

connection_types.name: dendritic_excitatory_synapse
connection_types.description: Excitatory contact placed on a specific dendritic branch; branch-local integration.

connection_types.name: dendritic_inhibitory_synapse
connection_types.description: Inhibitory contact on a dendritic branch; vetoes a branch without somatic shunting.

connection_types.name: autapse_recurrent
connection_types.description: A population connects to itself with a gain < 1; local persistence without a loop node.

connection_types.name: feedforward_excitatory
connection_types.description: A -> B -> C all excitatory; signal relayed and sharpened across stages.

connection_types.name: feedforward_inhibitory
connection_types.description: Input excites both a target and an interneuron that inhibits the target; narrows the time window.

connection_types.name: feedforward_gating
connection_types.description: A gating population multiplicatively admits or blocks a throughput path.

connection_types.name: feedback_excitatory
connection_types.description: Higher stage re-excites an earlier stage; sustains and amplifies a representation.

connection_types.name: feedback_inhibitory
connection_types.description: Higher stage returns inhibition to an earlier stage; predictive suppression.

connection_types.name: lateral_inhibitory
connection_types.description: Neighbouring units inhibit each other; sharpens contrast and sparsifies the code.

connection_types.name: lateral_feedback
connection_types.description: Lateral partner both feeds forward and receives feedback; forms a resonant ring.

connection_types.name: mutual_inhibitory
connection_types.description: Two populations inhibit each other; produces winner-take-all or alternation.

connection_types.name: recurrent_excitatory
connection_types.description: Population excites itself through a loop; attractor / persistent activity.

connection_types.name: recurrent_inhibitory
connection_types.description: Loop where inhibition dominates; keeps activity bounded and rhythmic.

connection_types.name: disinhibition
connection_types.description: A -> interneuron -| target: exciting the interneuron releases the target.

connection_types.name: shunting_inhibition
connection_types.description: Inhibition lowers input resistance rather than hyperpolarising; divisive gain control.

connection_types.name: contrast_inhibition
connection_types.description: Inhibition proportional to local stimulus energy; normalises the population response.

connection_types.name: winner_take_all
connection_types.description: Global inhibitory pool lets the strongest unit suppress the rest; selection operator.

connection_types.name: loop_relay_chain
connection_types.description: Strictly ordered series of relays; each stage passes a transformed copy onward.

connection_types.name: modulatory_diffuse
connection_types.description: One modulatory source broadcasts a scalar gain over many targets; no point-to-point map.

connection_types.name: neuromodulatory_axon
connection_types.description: Axon with en-passant varicosities releasing along its length, not at one terminal.

connection_types.name: volume_transmission
connection_types.description: Transmitter diffuses through extracellular space and reaches non-synaptic receptors.

connection_types.name: short_range_volume
connection_types.description: Locally confined diffusion; a middle case between a synapse and full volume release.

connection_types.name: retrograde_messenger
connection_types.description: Postsynaptic cell releases a messenger that acts back on the presynaptic terminal.

connection_types.name: state_gating_modulation
connection_types.description: A global state variable (arousal, phase) multiplies whole-pathway throughput.

connection_types.name: gap_junction_sync
connection_types.description: Bidirectional electrotonic coupling; equalises membrane potential, zero delay.

connection_types.name: gap_junction_inhibitory
connection_types.description: Gap junction onto an inhibitory population; synchronises the local brake.

connection_types.name: ephaptic_coupling
connection_types.description: Non-synaptic field coupling; activity in one fibre changes the excitability of a neighbour. Span is 'either', because a field does not respect a unit boundary -- an electric organ drives its own receptors across tissues.

connection_types.name: astrocyte_neuron_tripartite
connection_types.description: Astrocyte senses synaptic activity and returns a slow modulatory signal.

connection_types.name: gliotransmission_calcium_wave
connection_types.description: Calcium wave propagates through the astrocytic syncytium, carrying a slow signal.

connection_types.name: stdp_rule
connection_types.description: Pre-before-post potentiates, post-before-pre depresses; timing-based weight change.

connection_types.name: ltp_ltd
connection_types.description: Sustained activity produces durable bidirectional weight change.

connection_types.name: short_term_plasticity
connection_types.description: Vesicle depletion / residual calcium give seconds-scale facilitation or depression.

connection_types.name: dendritic_computation
connection_types.description: Non-linear dendritic integration (NMDA spikes, plateau potentials) as a local operator.

connection_types.name: homeostatic_scaling
connection_types.description: Slow multiplicative rescaling of all weights to hold a firing-rate set-point.

connection_types.name: topographic_mapping
connection_types.description: Spatially ordered projection preserving neighbourhood relations across stages.

connection_types.name: temporal_coherence
connection_types.description: Co-active populations phase-align; binding by synchrony rather than by weight.

connection_types.name: inhibitory_hub
connection_types.description: A single inhibitory hub broadcasts to a very large target set (MaleCNS-extracted).

connection_types.name: reservoir_smallworld
connection_types.description: High-clustering, short-path recurrent pool used as a random-feature reservoir (MaleCNS-extracted).

connection_types.name: recurrent_feedback
connection_types.description: Closed loop between two stages with a delay; the MaleCNS-extracted third original motif.

connection_types.name: divergent_fanout
connection_types.description: One source drives many independent downstream populations; broadcast without feedback.

connection_types.name: convergent_fanin
connection_types.description: Many sources converge onto one target; the target sees an integrated sum.

connection_types.name: corollary_discharge
connection_types.description: A copy of a motor command is routed to a sensory/predictor unit alongside the action.

connection_types.name: global_broadcast
connection_types.description: A command reaches every unit in the organism; used for reset, halt, or global gain.

connection_types.name: sparse_expansion_projection
connection_types.description: A few input channels fan out onto a very large population of which only a small fraction is active per stimulus -- the mushroom-body Kenyon-cell code.
connection_types.biological_reference: Turner et al 2008; Caron et al 2013

connection_types.name: global_inhibitory_gain_control
connection_types.description: One wide-field inhibitory cell sums the whole population and feeds back onto all of it, enforcing sparseness (APL onto Kenyon cells).

connection_types.name: neural_chain_sequence
connection_types.description: A synfire-like chain in which each element activates the next after a short delay, turning a static command into a temporal sequence (HVC song timing).
connection_types.biological_reference: Long et al 2010; Picardo et al 2016

connection_types.name: efference_copy_cancellation
connection_types.description: A copy of the motor command is sent ahead to sensory areas and subtracted from the reafferent input, so self-generated signals are not mistaken for the world (electric-fish EOD; song auditory feedback).

connection_types.name: mixed_electrical_chemical_synapse
connection_types.description: A contact carrying both a gap-junction conductance and a chemical component; this is what gives the Mauthner cell its sub-millisecond all-or-none drive.

connection_types.name: modulatory_gated_plasticity
connection_types.description: A synapse whose weight changes only when a third, modulatory neuron is co-active: local learning requires a global reinforcement signal (DAN onto the Kenyon-cell output synapse).
connection_types.biological_reference: Aso et al 2014; Cognigni et al 2018

connection_types.name: repetitive_activation_lts
connection_types.description: A brief run of presynaptic spikes produces a lasting increase in release that outlives the train by many minutes -- the cephalopod vertical-lobe rule.

connection_types.name: command_neuron_recruitment
connection_types.description: One identified command neuron, once past threshold, recruits an entire downstream motor pool all-or-none (Mauthner cell; EOD pacemaker nucleus).

connection_types.name: half_center_oscillation
connection_types.description: Two reciprocally inhibitory pools plus adaptation: whichever is releasing the other from inhibition takes the next half-cycle, so a tonic drive becomes an alternating rhythm with no cell being intrinsically rhythmic (leech swim CPG; respiratory pre-Botzinger).
connection_types.biological_reference: Marder & Calabrese 1996; Friesen 1989; Kristan et al 2005

connection_types.name: plateau_potential_bistability
connection_types.description: A brief input pushes the cell onto a sustained depolarised plateau that outlives the stimulus by hundreds of milliseconds; this is what gives a CPG its commitment and its hysteresis.

connection_types.name: serotonergic_presynaptic_facilitation
connection_types.description: A modulatory terminal raises release probability in the sensory neuron without any postsynaptic depolarisation -- the mechanism of sensitisation in the Aplysia gill-withdrawal reflex, i.e. a memory stored presynaptically.

connection_types.name: short_term_habituation
connection_types.description: Repeated activation of the same pathway depresses release, so the same stimulus produces a progressively smaller response and recovers in minutes -- the counterweight to presynaptic facilitation.
connection_types.biological_reference: Castellucci et al 1970; Rankin et al 2009

connection_types.name: coincidence_detection
connection_types.description: The synapse only changes when two inputs arrive together: a single climbing fibre carrying the error must coincide with parallel-fibre activity for the Purkinje synapse to depress. Teaching, not correlation.
connection_types.biological_reference: Ito & Kano 1982; Ito 1984; De Zeeuw et al 2011

connection_types.name: state_switch_bistable
connection_types.description: Two mutually inhibitory populations with a slow external bias: the circuit sits in one of two stable states and a small, brief input flips the whole thing, which is how sleep/wake cannot sit halfway.
connection_types.biological_reference: Saper et al 2005; Saper et al 2010

connection_types.name: grid_phase_precession
connection_types.description: A theta-rhythm reference makes a spatial cell's firing phase advance linearly with distance travelled, converting a place code into a temporal code -- the mechanism that lets position be read out by spike timing.
connection_types.biological_reference: O'Keefe & Recce 1993; Hafting et al 2005; Burgess et al 2007

connection_types.name: thermal_cross_modal_convergence
connection_types.description: An infrared map and a visual map registered onto the same tectal neurons, so a warm target is localised in the same coordinates as a seen one and either modality can drive the strike (pit vipers; vampire bats).
connection_types.biological_reference: Hartline et al 2011; Gracheva et al 2010; Newman & Hartline 1982
